subject: Re: DPA – backup deletion windows & log retention exceptions
messages:
From: Acme Corp DPO <dpo@acme.com>

Cc: Acme SecOps <secops@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify backup deletion windows and DPA alignment

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending the DPA draft. Before we proceed, our security team needs clear alignment on a couple of operational items that affect our obligations under EU data protection law and our internal retention rules:

- Backups: what is Redwood's maximum window for deleting customer data from backups after a data deletion request? The DPA currently says "reasonable efforts" for backup purge; we need a concrete SLA or timeline (e.g., 30/60/90 days) or an explicit exclusion.
- Deletion workflows: please outline the steps (who triggers, verification, and audit logging) when a customer requests deletion of account data vs. deletion of logs/telemetry.
- Log retention exceptions: are there categories of logs (security forensics, billing) that are retained beyond standard retention and if so how are those scoped and purged?

We'd like a brief write-up we can attach to our records and send to our legal team. If CloudVault (your backup vendor) is used, please include their subprocessor role and any transfer/legal basis.

Thanks,
Priya Rao

Karthik / Priya —

I reviewed the DPA and drafted two precise options we can offer for the backup purge language (attached as a redline):

Option A (operational SLA): "Following a verified deletion request, Redwood Inference will purge the customer's data from primary storage immediately and remove customer-identifiable data from backups within 60 days, subject to CloudVault's snapshot lifecycle and any legal hold requirements."

Option B (limited exclusion + audit): "Customer data will be removed from backups within 180 days due to immutable snapshot windows; Redwood will maintain an auditable record of deletion requests and provide the customer with confirmation once backup purging completes."

Notes:
- 60 days is tighter and better for privacy posture but may require changing snapshot frequency and/or retention at CloudVault.
- 180 days is conservative and reflects our current worst-case with replication and cross-region snapshots.
- We should explicitly carve out logs required for security forensics and billing (describe categories and maximum retention in an appendix).

Suggested action: Grace to confirm operational feasibility of 60-day purge and list any categories of logs that must be retained longer (with retention maxima). If 60 days is not feasible, we offer 90 or 180 as compromise and include an audit/notification commitment.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi all — operational details below so you can pick language: we run daily snapshots with a 30-day rolling window in primary region and weekly cross-region snapshots retained for compliance for an additional period. CloudVault's immutable snapshots commit retention increments on replication and require a minimum of 7 days to start a purge job; coordination with their support is required for forced purge.

Concrete listing:
- Primary data stores: deletion request -> data flagged and removed from live indexes within 24 hours; background jobs scrub references within 72 hours.
- Local snapshots (daily): retained 30 days; purge job can be scheduled immediately after a verified deletion but will take up to 7 days to execute against snapshot catalog.
- Cross-region snapshots (weekly replication): retained 90 days in current configuration; purge of replicated snapshots requires CloudVault coordination and can add up to an additional 30 days operationally.
- Immutable forensic logs: retained up to 12 months for security/audit purposes; these logs are hashed and access-limited.

Putting that together, practical worst-case timelines: purge from primary/live: 24–72 hours; remove from backups/snapshots: 37–120 days depending on whether cross-region replication is involved and whether CloudVault needs manual intervention.

We can commit to Option B with a capped maximum of 120 days for full deletion from all backups (including cross-region), and provide an interim confirmation at 30 days when local snapshots are cleared. If Acme requires 60 days maximum, we will need to (a) change CloudVault snapshot retention on your tenant to accelerate cross-region snap expiry and (b) accept a small operational fee to cover expedited operations and manual purge coordination.

Operational ask for Acme: confirm whether you need the 60-day SLA or the 120-day capped commitment, and whether you'd like Redwood to initiate the CloudVault retention change (we'll include instructions & an SOW).

Grace O'Connor
Head of Production Engineering, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

Attachment: backup-retention-matrix.xlsx

Karthik / Rishi / Grace — thanks for the detailed responses and the redline. Acme's position: we need a firm maximum for backup purge of 90 days for this engagement to meet our internal policy and customer commitments. The 120-day cap is acceptable only if accompanied by an automated notification when local snapshots clear (30 days) and a documented manual purge playbook.

We are willing to accept a $5k one-time onboarding fee to cover CloudVault coordination if that gets us to a 90-day hard cap. Please provide updated DPA language reflecting: (1) 90-day maximum for full backup purge post-verified deletion; (2) carveout for immutable forensic logs (max 12 months) with explicit notification procedures; (3) commitment to provide confirmation at 30 days and final confirmation once backups are purged.

If you can send the updated redline and the SOW for the CloudVault change by EOD Wednesday we will proceed to sign.

Best,
Priya Rao
Data Protection Officer, Acme Corp
